paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: becoming a new person isn't about trying harder with the same old self. It's about a swap. Paul says to put off your former way of life, your old self, and to put on the new self, "created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness" (Ephesians 4:22, 24). And the middle step is the secret sauce: being "renewed in the spirit of your minds" (Ephesians 4:23).

Now look at what the swap looks like in real life, because Paul doesn't leave it floating in the clouds. Lies get replaced with truth, and Paul's reason is "for we are all members of one another" (Ephesians 4:25). The one who was taking starts working so he can give (Ephesians 4:28). Words that tear down get replaced with words that build up (Ephesians 4:29). Every time something comes OFF, something better goes ON, and that's the whole pattern!

And here's why it matters to you: Paul says you can do this because you're not starting from scratch. You were "sealed for the day of redemption" in the Holy Spirit, so don't grieve Him (Ephesians 4:30). Then comes the line that holds the whole thing together: "Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you" (Ephesians 4:32). I think that's the best part, friend, because you're not forgiving from empty hands. You're passing along what you were already handed.
